Our final sample has
14,256 firm-year observations.
Table 2 tabulates descriptive statistics for the overall sample. All variables are
scaled by lagged total assets. We report mean (median) net income of - 2.6 percent
(3.7 percent) and mean (median) cash flow of 3.0 percent (6.8 percent). Our sample
firms are less profitable than those examined in Subramanyam’s 1996 large-scale
study of discretionary accruals. For his sample spanning the period 1973–93, he
reports mean (median) net income of 5.3 percent (5.7 percent) and mean (median)
cash flow of 8.8 percent (9.4 percent). This difference may be due to his requirement
that sample firms have five consecutive years of data to estimate discretionary accruals, while our study does not require consecutive data. The different time period
may also be related to the overall level of profitability. Nondiscretionary accruals
are negative, as expected, and have a mean (median) of - 4.1 percent ( - 3.5 percent). Unexpected total accruals ( UTACC ) have a mean (median) value of - 1.5
percent ( - 0.3 percent), with 48 percent of firms reporting positive values.

Consistent with our expectations, reported medians for all of our unexpected
specific accruals except one are close to zero, with the percent positive ranging
from 48 percent to 52 percent. This suggests that our method for estimating the
expected values of these variables is reasonable. The exception is special items,
which has a zero median but a mean of - 1.9 percent. This is consistent with Kinney
and Trezevant 1997, who also report a negative mean for special items. However,
firms often report no special items; in our sample special items are zero for over
half of the firm-years. We therefore retain our measure of unexpected special items
but also report sensitivity tests regarding this variable in section 5.

Table 3 presents Pearson correlation coefficients between the Jones 1991
model unexpected total accruals measure, UTACC, and our specific accrual measures.
All specific measures are significantly correlated with UTACC in the directions
expected: UAR, UINV, and USI are significantly positively correlated, and UAP,
UACCL, and UDEP are significantly negatively correlated. However, these correlations, ranging from - 0.15 to 0.48, and the correlations between specific accruals

result of the Jones 1991 model’s not attempting to incorporate special items into its

Overall, Table 3 suggests that our measures reasonably capture the unexpected
portion of the specific accruals, that they are all significantly related to unexpected total
accruals, and that special items have an especially strong relationship with unexpected
total accruals.
